records.issue_text: [BUG] The `queued` field default is `timezone.now()` evaluated once at class-definition (import) time, so every AssignmentSource instance records the process import time, not the actual queue time. Any future use of `queued` for staleness/debugging measures against a timestamp frozen at worker boot; all instances share one value.
records.rationale: In `AssignmentSource` the dataclass field is declared as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` (new file `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`). That expression is evaluated at import/class-definition time, so all `AssignmentSource()` instances created without explicitly passing `queued` will share the same timestamp (the time the module was imported), rather than the creation time. This matches the finding; the correct pattern would be `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The `queued` field's default is `timezone.now()` evaluated once at module import, so every AssignmentSource created in a process shares the same process-start timestamp. Dataclass defaults are evaluated at class-definition time, not per-instantiation: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` runs when assignment_source.py is first imported. All sources built via from_integration carry the worker process's boot time rather than the actual assignment time, so any future use of `queued` for staleness/cycle detection (its only plausible purpose) computes wrong ages — e.g., a long-lived region-silo worker stamps every inbound sync with hours-old timestamps. The author's likely counter is that `queued` is currently unused downstream; but shipping a field whose value is wrong by construction guarantees misinterpretation the moment someone reads it. Fix is mechanical: use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.
